questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It is an English-speaking country and they have some interesting classes.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite hard to find information about my exchange. We waited a lot for information and found out it was because there was nothing more we needed to do about the applications to the host university. We just thought we had to do more. So, it was a little confusing. It would have been nice with a schedule of what to do after we had been accepted to the host university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: At the university campus, we had some days where we got an introduction to the place and how it would be for an exchange student to be at Western University.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Needed more activity to meet other international students. Maybe a trip or something else than only one presentation and one international cafe.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was not hard, actually easier than expected. 
Look at Airbnb's that you can rent for the month you are here.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You have to make an extra effort to meet people because you don't live on campus with everybody else. 
Find a house between the city centre and the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is very expensive to live on and off campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very complicated.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you had to find the course on the course catalog but it is very different from Denmark, so the courses was address numbers and a letter. Then we had to find out what the different numbers and letters meant and a lot of the courses had pre-request and then you had to compare them to the classes you have had in Denmark. But overall we got the courses that we wanted and there is a group of people assigned to the international students who where very helpfull.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A whole team where assigned to help us. We could just send a email and they will reply very fast and helpfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful. I ended up with classes that I wanted after I had applied two times.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep an eye on the deadlines and use the international team assigned to help if you are in doubt about anything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The 4000-level courses match the courses in the third year of the BA.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Here the grade depends on more than only the final exam like on KU.
The grade here depends on participation, assignments, quizzes, midterms, and final exams. Sometimes more things like presentation also.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Microbiology and immunology 2500 A/B.
Psychology as a natural science 1002 A/B.
The principle of human genetics, biology 3592 A.
The Biology of Aging: Cellular and Molecular Aspects, biology 4355 F.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the biology of aging and the principle of human genetics. Micro/Immuno was also okay but not as good as the two other classes.

questions.answer: We had to buy some kitchen gear that were not included.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The living expenses were higher than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Gym is free when you are a student at Western University.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Gym classes if you like to go to classes like spinning. 
Outdoor clubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
See Montreal, Toronto, Banff, Vancouver, Niagara Falls, New York, etc. 
Especially see Banff and the beautiful nature. If you miss Europe a little go to Montreal.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. There are some differences but they are small.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to participate as much as you can and when you meet people try to get their contact information.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There are a lot more homeless people in Canada than in Denmark. People are a lot more open over here and chatty.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live close to campus or the city.
Participate in as much as you can to meet people. 
Be prepared for people being a bit younger than you.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: People are nice and open.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The ability to explore Canada and meet nice people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is a lot different and you have to get used to always following up on deadlines for quizzes, assignments, articles, etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It is a big opportunity and I would recommend going on an exchange. It is a nice way to explore a new country and culture meanwhile you are studying.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
